newsitem.title: USA: UAW hits GM with two more strike deadlines.
newsitem.headline: UAW hits GM with two more strike deadlines.

text.p: The United Auto Workers union hit General Motors Corp. with two more strike deadlines Friday, the second time in two days the UAW has set the stage for potentially crippling work stoppages at key parts plants.

GM officials said the automaker received notice that strike deadlines were set for 11:59 p.m. EDT on June 13 at its Saginaw Malleable Iron plant in Saginaw, Mich., and its Grand Rapids, Mich. metal stamping plant.

About 900 hourly workers affiliated with UAW Local 455 work at the Saginaw plant, and 2,346 hourly workers from UAW Local 730 are at the stamping facility, where sheet metal is pressed into auto parts.

On Thursday, the UAW issued a June 12 strike deadline for GM's catalytic converter plant in suburban Milwaukee. The facility makes converters for nearly all of GM's North American-built cars and trucks and exports to GM's Adam Opel AG unit in Germany.
UAW spokesman Reg McGhee said neither of the Michigan locals have new contracts with GM. He said the strike deadlines were set because of unresolved grievances.

At issue in both disputes are health and safety concerns, as well as production standards, a category that includes production line speed and staffing levels. McGhee declined to say if the locals want GM to add more jobs, a regular union demand in the ongoing labour strife at GM.

McGhee said the timing of the strike deadlines reflected a desire by the UAW's top leaders to get long-simmering contract disputes resolved. "These are local union contracts that have been going on for nearly a year and we just wanted to get them resolved," he said.

About 20 of GM's more than 100 UAW locals do not have local agreements, although a new national pact was signed last November. A steady trickle of strikes has plagued the world's largest automaker since January, hurting the introduction of new models and the supply of popular truck demand.

GM continues to battle a 45-day-old strike by 5,800 workers at its Pontiac East, Mich., pickup truck plant. Last month, the company settled a seven-week walkout at its Oklahoma City, Okla., car plant.

A work stoppage at the casting plant could severely curtail GM's light truck production within a week, said Michael Robinet, managing director of CSM Forecasting, an industry consultant in Farmington Hills, Mich.
"This is the major source for truck engine blocks," he said. "It would be a major hurdle for General Motors to continue truck operations past a week."

The Saginaw facility, which is part of GM's Powertrain Group, also makes connecting rods, pistons, truck hubs, yokes and transmission components for GM and non-GM customers, said GM spokeswoman Darla Park.

The Grand Rapids stamping plant is part of GM's Metal Fabricating division. Spokesman Peter Ternes said the facility makes major metal stampings for doors, floor pans, rear ends, and quarter panels. He declined to say what vehicle lines it supplies, but added: "It produces quite a few stampings for a number of products."
GM stock edged up 12.5 cents to $56.875 on the New York Stock Exchange.
